definitions.explanation: Intensely blue in color, typically describing sky or sea.
Having lost color in the face due to shock, fear, or illness.

examples.japanese: {真|ま}っ{青|さお}な{空|そら}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: A deep blue sky spread out before us.

examples.japanese: その{知|し}らせを{聞|き}いて、{顔|かお}が{真|ま}っ{青|さお}になった。
examples.english: Upon hearing the news, my face turned pale.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}が{真|ま}っ{青|さお}で{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The sea was a beautiful deep blue.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{真|ま}っ (emphatic prefix) + {青|あお}→{青|さお} (blue)
Note the sound change from あお to さお.

TWO MEANINGS:
This word has seemingly opposite meanings:
1. Deep, vivid blue (positive)
2. Pale, ashen (negative - loss of color from fear/shock)

Context makes the meaning clear.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{顔|かお}が{真|ま}っ{青|さお}になる - to turn pale (from shock/fear)
・{真|ま}っ{青|さお}な{空|そら} - deep blue sky
・{真|ま}っ{青|さお}な{海|うみ} - deep blue sea

RELATED:
・{真|ま}っ{赤|か} - bright red (also used for "blatant")
・{青|あお}ざめる - to turn pale
